editorial.headline: Crumb Rubber Manufacturing Stands Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22123 covers rubber processing that produces crumb rubber, with access across all recorded business scales and no Bali PMA block in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22123 is a focused manufacturing classification: the processing of rubber to produce crumb rubber. The record does not widen the activity beyond that point. Its centre of gravity is industrial transformation, not trading, plantation work, or downstream product claims. For a founder, that makes the code relatively clean to read: it is about the factory-side activity that turns rubber into crumb rubber, and the registration should be judged on that precise scope.

The scale position is unusually broad in the supplied record. The activity is marked open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the code is not confined to a single size of operator. A small processor and a larger industrial setup are both visible within the scale field, although the record itself does not add any threshold, facility requirement, production volume, or capital figure. Those details would have to come from another verified source before they could be treated as compliance facts.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clear. Nationally, PMA status is TERBUKA, with the maximum foreign ownership recorded at 100%. In plain terms, the national record treats this crumb rubber manufacturing activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full ceiling shown here. The source attached to that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the slim record adds a special national licence condition, ownership partner requirement, or reduced foreign stake, so none should be inferred.

The Bali reading is also important because this is where many open national classifications become practically unavailable for PMA registration. For Bali, the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK; the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. That means the Bali moratorium is relevant context, but not a block for this record. The moratorium rule says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently; this code, as recorded here, is not caught by that block. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: KBLI 22123 is nationally open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali record supplied here does not block PMA registration.
